method: Live sweep of classroom.google.com/?hl=<tag> in a logged-in desktop session. For each requested tag, document.documentElement.lang (the value the extension's language resolver sees) plus sidebar/title strings were captured from the real page. Classroom honors ?hl= per request without touching account settings.
keyFindings: Google serves the LEGACY code iw for Hebrew — the iw->he alias is load-bearing on real traffic.
es-419 is served as its own tag; pt requests are served as pt-BR; region tags (en-US, en-GB, pt-BR, pt-PT, zh-CN, zh-TW, es-419) all appear in real docLang values.
Google strips script subtags: sr-Latn request is served as sr (Cyrillic only).

Classroom does NOT ship in 40+ languages the extension translates (am, zu, so, yo, ha, ig, mt, mi, st, sn, sd, ny, yi, eo, haw, to, ia, ak, bem, ee, gaa, kg->fr, ...) — those pages render en-US, or a regional fallback (mg/kg/ln/lua/rw/wo/br/co/oc/crs/ht -> fr, su/jw/jv -> id, tg -> ru, la -> it, rm -> de, fo -> da, fy -> nl, ay/gn/qu/gl -> es, sa/bho -> hi, ku -> tr, ckb -> ar, nn/nb -> no, bs -> hr, ceb -> fil, gd -> en-GB).
Real Google UI keeps product names English in several fully-served languages (Calendar in es, ko, pa, te, mr, ml, ms) — shared-vocab with English can be the correct localization.

knownGaps: Post-level strings (Posted, (Edited), Add class comment, N class comments, Stream/Classwork tabs) could not be captured in the automation browser: Classroom's main content pane fails to render there (blank main region while the sidebar works). Capture those from a regular logged-in Chrome via the existing tests/accuracy corpus workflow.
